objects.description: Enumeration of output formatting styles for Sass rendering. Values control how compiled CSS is formatted (nested, expanded, compact, compressed) and include internal/inspection styles. No additional metadata or functions are provided here.

Opaque/forward-declared union representing any Sass value (number, string, color, list, map, boolean, null, error, warning). Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the layout is hidden. Manipulate via the provided API. Lifetime is heap-allocated via sass_make_* constructors and must be released with sass_delete_value. Lists and maps are recursively owned and freed by sass_delete_value.

objects.definition:
enum Sass_Tag {
  SASS_BOOLEAN,
  SASS_NUMBER,
  SASS_COLOR,
  SASS_STRING,
  SASS_LIST,
  SASS_MAP,
  SASS_NULL,
  SASS_ERROR,
  SASS_WARNING
};
objects.description: Enumeration of the concrete kind/tag of a Sass_Value. Use with sass_value_get_tag and type predicates to determine the actual contained type.
Enumeration of list separators for Sass list values (comma, space). SASS_HASH is an internal sentinel used pre-evaluation to denote a hash-like separator.
Enumeration of supported value operations for sass_value_op, including logical, relational, and arithmetic operators. NUM_OPS marks the enum size.
Opaque/forward-declared environment frame used to access lexical, local, and global Sass variables during callbacks. Only a forward declaration is present here; managed by the Sass runtime.
Opaque callee descriptor representing the current callable context (mixin/function/C function). Only forward-declared here; queried via sass_callee_get_* APIs.
Opaque import entry describing a single import result (path, source, source map, or an error). Only forward-declared here; constructed and owned via the import APIs in this header.
Opaque options/configuration object for the Sass compiler. Forward declaration only; defined elsewhere.
Opaque compiler instance passed into importer and function callbacks. Forward declaration only; created/managed by the broader Sass API, not in this header.
Opaque importer callback descriptor that encapsulates a custom importer function, priority, and cookie. Forward-declared here; created and managed via make/delete functions in this header.
Opaque custom function callback descriptor holding a signature, function pointer, and cookie. Forward-declared; created and managed via make/delete functions in this header.

Pointer-to-function type returning a pointer to an array/list of Sass_Import entries. Used as the return type of custom importer callbacks. Note: This is a function pointer type, not a list container itself.

Pointer-to-function type representing a list of Sass_Importer entries. Used by APIs constructing/manipulating importer lists. Note: This is a function pointer typedef in this header’s ABI; treated as the list handle in APIs.

objects.definition:
typedef Sass_Import_List (*Sass_Importer_Fn)
  (const char* url, Sass_Importer_Entry cb, struct Sass_Compiler* compiler);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom importer callbacks. Given a URL, the importer entry (self), and compiler, returns a Sass_Import_List describing zero or more imports or an error entry.
Pointer-to-function type representing a list of Sass_Function entries; serves as the list handle in the function list APIs.

objects.definition:
typedef union Sass_Value* (*Sass_Function_Fn)
  (const union Sass_Value*, Sass_Function_Entry cb, struct Sass_Compiler* compiler);
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom Sass function implementations. Accepts the argument list (Sass_Value), the function entry (self), and compiler; returns a Sass_Value result (ownership rules defined by the Sass API elsewhere).
Enumeration identifying the type of the current callee context: a mixin, a Sass function, or a native C function.

Alias for a pointer-to-function typedef referencing a Sass_Env frame used by environment getters/setters in this header. Note: This is an alias form used by the API; underlying type is struct Sass_Env (opaque).
Alias typedef for a Sass callee descriptor pointer used throughout the callee APIs.
Alias typedef for a Sass import entry pointer.
Alias typedef for a Sass importer descriptor pointer.
Alias typedef for a Sass function descriptor pointer.
Opaque compiler handle for libsass. Forward-declared only in this header; actual structure is private. Represents a compiler instance that can parse and/or execute a compilation pipeline.
Opaque options object holding compilation configuration (precision, style, paths, source map flags, callbacks, etc.). Forward-declared here; real definition is private.
Opaque base context for a compilation run. Carries results (CSS, source map, errors) and references options. Forward-declared here; concrete layout is private.
Opaque context for file-based compilation (input is a path). Derived from Sass_Context conceptually; defined privately elsewhere.
Opaque context for data/string-based compilation (input is in-memory source). Conceptually derived from Sass_Context; defined privately elsewhere.
Enumeration of the libsass compiler lifecycle states: just created, parsed, or executed.

State holder used by the C++ sass2scss converter within namespace Sass. Tracks formatting and parsing state (options, selector context, list concatenation, property/semicolon flags), comment context, EOF, buffered whitespace, and an indentation/context stack. Construction is implicit via aggregate initialization; no special constructors or destructors are defined beyond those of its STL members.

functions.name: sass_alloc_memory
functions.signature: ADDAPI void* ADDCALL sass_alloc_memory(size_t size);
functions.description: Allocates a raw memory buffer of the requested size using libsass’s allocator (useful for crossing DLL boundaries). Use sass_free_memory to release this buffer. Intended for callers who need a buffer to pass into libsass or to interoperate with memory libsass will later manage.
requirements: size must be the number of bytes to allocate (non-negative; size_t range)
The returned pointer must be freed with sass_free_memory (not free/delete)
The returned pointer may be NULL on allocation failure (check before use)
The memory is uninitialized unless otherwise documented

requirements: str should be a valid, null-terminated C string
The returned pointer must be freed with sass_free_memory (not free/delete)
Behavior when str is NULL is unspecified by this header (treat as unknown)

functions.name: sass_free_memory
functions.signature: ADDAPI void ADDCALL sass_free_memory(void* ptr);
functions.description: Frees memory that was allocated via libsass allocation helpers (e.g., sass_alloc_memory or buffers returned by libsass APIs). Use this to release any memory ‘overtaken’ or returned by libsass.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously allocated by sass_alloc_memory or returned by a libsass API that specifies sass_free_memory for cleanup
Do not pass pointers allocated by standard allocators (malloc/new)
Do not free the same pointer more than once
Behavior for ptr == NULL is not specified by this header (treat as unknown)

requirements: str should be a valid, null-terminated C string
quote_mark is the desired quote character; typical values are '"' or '\'' (exact accepted set is not specified here)
The returned pointer must be freed with sass_free_memory
Behavior when str is NULL is unspecified by this header

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces interesting, but valid, NUL-terminated strings for libsass APIs.
# It targets stubs that consume arbitrary C strings and filenames. We therefore build a
# SCSS/SASS-relevant corpus and then vary it deterministically based on the seed.

_MAX_LEN = 1024  # keep well below 4096 cap

_BASE_STRINGS: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty
    "a",  # single char
    "hello",
    "world\n",  # includes newline
    "\"quoted string\"",
    "'single quoted'",
    "`backtick`",
    "url(\"http://example.com\")",
    "line1\nline2\nline3\n",
    "tab\tseparated\tvalues",
    "comma,separated,list",
    " space leading",
    "trailing space ",
    " multiple   spaces ",
    r"escapes\\n\\t\\r",
    "#id .class > child { color: red; }",
    "$var: 10px;",
    "@mixin center($w) { width: $w; margin: 0 auto; }",
    "@include center(100px);",
    "$map: (a: 1, b: 2);",
    "@function add($a, $b) { @return $a + $b; }",
    ".btn { padding: 1rem 2rem; }",
    ".grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr; }",
    "@import 'foo';",
    "@use 'bar' as b; .x { color: b.$c; }",
    "/* block comment */",
    "// line comment\n$color: #abc;",
    "$n: 1.23456789e3;",
    "calc(100% - 10px)",
    "content: 'a\\'b';",
    "content: \"a\\\"b\";",
    "[data-attr~='val'] { color: blue; }",
    "@if true { a: b; } @else { c: d; }",
    "@for $i from 1 through 3 { .n-#{$i} { z: $i; } }",
    "@each $k, $v in (a:1,b:2) { .#{$k} { n:$v; } }",
    "@while false { x: y; }",
]

# Filenames used by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(); provide simple and nested paths with extensions
_FILE_NAMES: List[str] = [
    "a.scss",
    "b.sass",
    "_partial.scss",
    "nested/dir/file.scss",
    "nested/dir/_partial.sass",
    "../rel/path.scss",
    "C:/abs/win/path.scss",
    "/abs/unix/path.sass",
    "mixins/_utilities.scss",
    "imports.scss",
]

# Additional unit-like or CSS tokens to mix into random strings
_TOKENS: List[str] = [
    "px", "em", "rem", "%", "vh", "vw", "deg", "rad", "s", "ms",
    "rgb(10,20,30)", "rgba(1,2,3,0.4)", "hsl(120, 50%, 50%)",
    "!important", "inherit", "initial", "unset",
    "--var", "var(--var)",
]

def _rand_range(rng: random.Random, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(lo, hi)

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Include a broad set that keeps NUL out (callee expects NUL-terminated C-strings)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \t\n\r"
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _build_interesting_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a base
    base = rng.choice(_BASE_STRINGS)

    # Optionally concatenate with filename-like or tokens
    parts = [base]

    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(" ")
        parts.append(rng.choice(_TOKENS))

    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(" ")
        parts.append(rng.choice(_FILE_NAMES))

    # Occasionally produce quoted variants for quote/unquote functions
    s = "".join(parts)
    mode = rng.randint(0, 5)
    if mode == 1:
        s = '"' + s + '"'
    elif mode == 2:
        s = "'" + s + "'"
    elif mode == 3:
        s = "`" + s + "`"
    elif mode == 4:
        # Embed some escapes
        s = s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"")
        s = '"' + s + '"'

    # Ensure length capped and add some random tail
    if len(s) < 64 and rng.random() < 0.8:
        s += _rand_ascii(rng, _rand_range(rng, 0, 32))

    if len(s) > _MAX_LEN:
        s = s[:_MAX_LEN]

    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide whether this buffer is intended as a filename or a general string
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        s = rng.choice(_FILE_NAMES)
        # Randomly nest directories or add relative bits
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            prefixes = ["./", "../", "/abs/", "nested/", "src/", "lib/"]
            s = rng.choice(prefixes) + s
        if len(s) < 40 and rng.random() < 0.4:
            s = s.replace(".scss", "") if s.endswith(".scss") else s
    else:
        s = _build_interesting_string(rng)

    # Guarantee NUL-terminated C string semantics when interpreted by C++ std::string::c_str()
    # Returning bytes without embedded NUL ensures stubs see full content; we do not include NUL in the buffer itself
    data = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path
# Goal: produce a bytes buffer that the harness will use for both FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# (a path to an existing temp file with random data) and FUZZ_PARAM_STR (generic strings).
# We therefore generate a small blob encoding one or more plausible path strings and
# optional SCSS/SASS-like content which the harness can slice to populate different
# calls. The buffer should be valid UTF-8, NUL-terminated substrings where useful,
# and under 4096 bytes.

# Strategy
# - Emit one primary path that looks realistic and covers cases: absolute/relative,
#   nested dirs, underscores, extensions used by Sass (.scss, .sass, .css, .map), partials (_file).
# - Include a second alternate path (e.g., for abs_base or source map path).
# - Provide inline text blocks that can serve as plausible SCSS/SASS source and sourcemap JSON.
# - Separate items with NUL bytes so consumers that expect C strings can safely read until NUL.
# - Keep total size < 4096.

PATH_SEPS = ["/", os.sep if os.sep != "/" else "/"]

EXTS = [
    "scss", "sass", "css", "map", "txt"
]

DIR_NAMES = [
    "src", "styles", "sass", "scss", "components", "partials", "vendor", "lib"
]

BASE_NAMES = [
    "main", "index", "app", "theme", "_variables", "_mixins", "_buttons", "_grid", "_colors"
]

def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(0, len(items))]

def rand_dir(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of given dir names and random tokens
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rand_choice(rng, DIR_NAMES)
    # random token
    token = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_-") for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)))
    return token

def rand_base(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rand_choice(rng, BASE_NAMES)
    token = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_-") for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12)))
    # sometimes underscore for partials
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and not token.startswith("_"):
        token = "_" + token
    return token

def rand_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rand_choice(rng, EXTS)

def build_path(rng: random.Random, absolute: bool) -> str:
    sep = rand_choice(rng, PATH_SEPS)
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(rand_dir(rng))
    base = rand_base(rng)
    # choose extension; bias to scss/sass for relevant APIs
    ext = rand_ext(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ext = rand_choice(rng, ["scss", "sass"])
    filename = f"{base}.{ext}"
    path_core = sep.join(parts + [filename]) if parts else filename
    if absolute:
        # Posix-like absolute to avoid Windows-specific oddities in harness
        if sep != "/":
            sep_use = "/"
        else:
            sep_use = "/"
        root = "/" if rng.random() < 0.85 else "/tmp"
        if not path_core:
            return root
        return root.rstrip("/") + sep_use + path_core
    else:
        # sometimes add ./ or ../ prefixes
        prefix = ""
        roll = rng.random()
        if roll < 0.2:
            prefix = "./"
        elif roll < 0.25:
            prefix = "../"
        return prefix + path_core

def make_sass_source(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce valid SCSS/SASS-like content
    # Keep length moderate
    colors = ["#123456", "#abcdef", "red", "rgba(10,20,30,0.5)"]
    units = ["px", "em", "rem", "%"]
    var1 = "$primary-color"
    var2 = "$space"
    n = rng.randint(4, 12)
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"{var1}: {rand_choice(rng, colors)};")
    lines.append(f"{var2}: {rng.randint(2,16)}{rand_choice(rng, units)};")
    lines.append("@mixin button($pad) { padding: $pad; color: #fff; background: #{" + var1 + "}; }")
    lines.append(".container { margin: 0 auto; width: 80%; }")
    lines.append(".grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: #{$space}; }")
    for i in range(n):
        cls = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(5))
        lines.append(f".{cls} {{ border: 1px solid {rand_choice(rng, colors)}; }}")
    lines.append(".btn { @include button($space); }")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def make_srcmap_json(rng: random.Random, sources: List[str]) -> str:
    # Minimal plausible source map JSON string
    # We do not attempt full encoding; lib may not parse it in these APIs, but keep it valid JSON
    version = 3
    file_name = rand_base(rng) + ".css"
    smap = {
        "version": version,
        "file": file_name,
        "sources": sources,
        "names": [],
        "mappings": ";;AACA;"
    }
    import json
    return json.dumps(smap, separators=(",", ":"))

def pack_c_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join strings as NUL-terminated segments, ending with a final NUL to be safe
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
        out += b + b"\x00"
    # ensure total size <= 4096
    if len(out) > 4096:
        return bytes(out[:4095] + b"\x00")
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build set of paths
    abs1 = build_path(rng, absolute=True)
    rel1 = build_path(rng, absolute=False)
    # A second absolute base path that looks like a directory, used as abs_base
    abs_dir = os.path.join("/", rand_dir(rng), rand_dir(rng))
    if not abs_dir.endswith("/"):
        abs_dir = abs_dir + "/"

    # Additional variants: underscore partial and map file
    partial = build_path(rng, absolute=False)
    if not os.path.basename(partial).startswith("_"):
        pdir = os.path.dirname(partial)
        pname, pext = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(partial))
        partial_name = "_" + (pname or "partial") + (pext or ".scss")
        partial = os.path.join(pdir, partial_name) if pdir else partial_name

    map_path = build_path(rng, absolute=False)
    root_like = "/styles/" + rand_base(rng) + ".scss"

    # Content blocks for s_src and s_map
    sass_src = make_sass_source(rng)
    sass_src_alt = make_sass_source(rng)
    srcmap = make_srcmap_json(rng, [rel1, partial])

    # Arrange segments in an order that matches common usage in stubs:
    # Many stubs first request a filename, then two strings (src, map). Others request
    # multiple filenames. We provide multiple NUL-terminated paths first, then text blocks.
    segments: List[str] = [
        abs1,
        rel1,
        abs_dir,
        partial,
        map_path,
        root_like,
        # Textual segments that may be copied into src/srcmap buffers
        sass_src,
        sass_src_alt,
        srcmap,
    ]

    return pack_c_strings(segments)
